subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a synchronous plugin-facing config pre-apply veto for persisted config writes, and what ordering, metadata, and failure semantics should it expose?
rationale: This is a security-sensitive public plugin API around auth, provider, channel, and gateway config writes; automation cannot choose fail-open/fail-closed behavior, recursion rules, actor metadata, or SecretRef/preflight ordering safely.

options.title: Design the API through the RFC path
options.body: Keep the issue open and require a maintainer-approved contract before implementation, including hook ordering, metadata, rejection shape, and tests proving rejected writes leave disk and active runtime config unchanged.

options.title: Scope to built-in validation only
options.body: Close or rescope the issue if maintainers decide plugin vetoes should not be able to block config persistence and core validation/doctor flows should own this boundary.

options.title: Limit to agent tool writes
options.body: Add a narrower config.patch/config.apply agent-tool guard, accepting that CLI/shared helper writes and other config mutators would remain outside the hook.

recommendation.title: Design the API through the RFC path
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and require a maintainer-approved contract before implementation, including hook ordering, metadata, rejection shape, and tests proving rejected writes leave disk and active runtime config unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already provided the maintainer review that kept this issue open and has recent adjacent config mutation history.
